R7 + R9 of the ultra review.

R7 -- Pl/Parser2.pm ~7089 (the ancestor walk's `next if ... Condition ... /^(?:if|unless|while|until)$/`, justified by "perl's local there lasts to the block end" -- TRUE for `if` / `unless` (RT #7615; perl-tests/local.t:862 TODO), NOT for loops).
  f7:  our $x = 'orig'; our @a = (1,2);
       { while (local $x = shift @a) { } print "in-block x=[", defined $x ? $x : 'undef', "]\n"; }  print "x=$x\n";
       perl: in-block x=[orig] / x=orig      base: x=[undef] / x= (NEVER restored)      MAIN: x=[undef] / x=orig (restored at block end only)
  FIX SHAPE: only the `if` / `unless` condition qualifies for the hoist; a `while` / `until` condition `local` refuses or announces (ruling 4) -- or lowers with a per-iteration restore if the loop lowering has a natural slot (probe `while (local $_ = shift @a) { ... }` -- the idiom perl programmers actually write -- vs perl first).  GUARD: f7's two prints (perl oracle), inverse-verified on fd04c048.

R9 -- Pl/Parser2.pm ~15189-15191: `_cond_mys_closure_captured` (#3374) reads as skipping an anon sub whose next token after `sub` is not the Block (signature / prototype / attribute) -- but f9 (`use v5.36; while (my $x = shift @q) { push @cbs, sub ($arg) { "$x:$arg" } }`) is perl-identical on main (`1:z,2:z,3:z`; the base read `:z,:z,:z`).  The prototype (`sub (&) {...}`) and attribute (`sub :lvalue {...}`) spellings were NOT probed: probe both vs perl; if they are right, say what makes them right (the Block is found through another path?) and CLOSE; if one is wrong, fix the token walk to skip the Signature / Prototype / Attribute tokens to the Block.


Related: #3370 (the lowering), #3414 (the announce residue), #3415 (nested-key local on the wrong slot), #3361 (data point 4: these sat on main; the instrument that found them was the cloud review, not a leg).  The fix batch: briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s520/s520b-prompt.md.

The keyword is found past a label; `!` / `not` before the term are inert.  `while (local $_ = shift @a)` probed first (perl: seen 1 2 3, after loop [top]; fd04c048 after loop [undef]; tree = perl).  f7 perl in-block x=[orig] / fd04c048 [undef] / tree [orig]. Guards rows 26-27.  corpus IDENTICAL.
